methodology: Human-labeled, held-out validation set for the duplicate/event-match judgment (FR-204/FR-205). Authored directly against the question 'do these two texts describe the same underlying incident, from roughly the same place and time?' -- NOT generated by rewriting HumAID/CrisisNLP tweets and NOT derived from or copied out of backend/app/services/seed_service.py's SEED_BATCH (DA-01), which exists for a different purpose (driving the live pipeline/replay demo, not measuring accuracy independently). Per docs/idea.md's honest-limitation note, any accuracy figure computed against this set should be reported as 'accuracy on a small human-labeled sample', never as 'dedup accuracy' unqualified, since 24 pairs is not a statistically powerful sample -- it exists to give one number that isn't self-fulfilling, not to replace broader evaluation. distance_km is the pre-computed haversine distance between the two reports' locations, mirroring FR-204's requirement that the LLM judge receive an explicit distance value rather than raw lat/lng. near_miss=true marks a non-duplicate pair that is lexically or topically similar (shares vocabulary, need-type, or a nearby-sounding description) despite describing a genuinely different incident -- these are the pairs that actually stress-test the judgment, as opposed to an easy contrast pair.

pairs.text_a: Our apartment block on Maple Terrace lost its roof in the storm, three families need emergency shelter tonight
pairs.text_b: Roof blew off the building on Maple Terrace during the storm, several of us have nowhere to sleep
pairs.note: Same building, same storm, same night -- corroborating witnesses.

pairs.text_a: Bridge over the Kandal river collapsed, cars are stuck on both sides
pairs.text_b: The river crossing near Kandal just went down, traffic trapped, need rescue crews
pairs.note: Same bridge collapse described from two vantage points.

pairs.text_a: Gas leak smell near the school on 4th, everyone's being told to evacuate
pairs.text_b: Evacuating the block near 4th street school, strong gas smell, some people feel dizzy
pairs.note: Same gas leak incident.

pairs.text_a: Landslide came down behind the clinic on Ridge Road, two houses buried
pairs.text_b: Mudslide hit houses right behind the Ridge Road clinic, people may be trapped inside
pairs.note: Same landslide, same reference landmark.

pairs.text_a: Power line came down on Elm and 2nd, sparking, nobody can get past
pairs.text_b: Downed power line sparking at the Elm/2nd intersection, road is blocked
pairs.note: Same downed line, same intersection.

pairs.text_a: Well water at the north camp has turned brown, kids are getting sick
pairs.text_b: The water from the well at north camp looks contaminated, several children have stomach illness
pairs.note: Same well, same contamination event, plausible distance within a camp.

pairs.text_a: Fishing boat capsized near the north jetty, two people still in the water
pairs.text_b: Boat overturned by the north jetty, we can see people struggling in the water
pairs.note: Same capsizing, same jetty.

pairs.text_a: Warehouse fire spreading fast on Dockside Ave, smoke is everywhere
pairs.text_b: Big fire at the Dockside Ave warehouse, embers landing on nearby roofs
pairs.note: Same fire, same street.

pairs.text_a: Sinkhole opened up on Baker Street outside the pharmacy, a car fell partway in
pairs.text_b: Ground gave way on Baker Street near the pharmacy, a vehicle is stuck in the hole
pairs.note: Same sinkhole.

pairs.text_a: Our shelter tent collapsed under the snow load, six of us need somewhere warm
pairs.text_b: Tent frame gave out from the snow at the same camp row, we're out in the cold now
pairs.note: Same weather event, adjacent tents, same camp row.

pairs.text_a: Grandmother had a stroke, left side went weak suddenly, we need an ambulance
pairs.text_b: My neighbor collapsed with stroke symptoms an hour ago, right where I reported the water outage earlier, still need help
pairs.note: Both are stroke reports in roughly the same area, but describe two different people/events an hour apart -- should not merge into one incident.

pairs.text_a: Need blankets for winter, household of five, otherwise doing okay
pairs.text_b: Requesting blankets and warm clothing for our family, we're fine but it's getting cold
pairs.note: Same need-type and near-identical phrasing, but 3.2km apart -- two unrelated households with the same generic ask, not one event.

pairs.text_a: House flooded on Birch Lane, water up to the windows, we're on the roof
pairs.text_b: Flooding on Birch Lane across town, ground floor is underwater, need a boat
pairs.note: Same street name recurs in two different parts of town (common in many cities) and same flood description -- but far enough apart to be a different flooded street, not corroboration.

pairs.text_a: Need insulin resupply by tonight, running dangerously low
pairs.text_b: My father's insulin runs out tomorrow morning, need it delivered before then
pairs.note: Same medical need-type and urgency shape, but different households and different timing -- not the same event.

pairs.text_a: Fire broke out at the market stalls on the east side, vendors evacuating
pairs.text_b: Small fire in a cooking stall near the west market, put out quickly, nobody hurt
pairs.note: Both fires, both markets, similar vocabulary -- but opposite sides of town and different severity/outcome.

pairs.text_a: Roof damaged in the wind, we're safe, would like a tarp when convenient
pairs.text_b: Storm knocked some tiles off our roof too, no rush, just need a tarp eventually
pairs.note: Same storm, same low-urgency roof-tarp ask, but different households far enough apart that they're independent low-priority requests, not one event.

pairs.text_a: Need clean water, none available for three days now
pairs.text_b: No access to safe drinking water since Tuesday, household of six
pairs.note: Same general shortage type in the same wider area (likely a regional supply problem) but different households, no shared specific location/landmark tying them together.

pairs.text_a: Elderly man next door can't walk to the distribution point, needs a home delivery
pairs.text_b: My elderly aunt across the valley also can't make it to a distribution point, needs supplies brought to her
pairs.note: Same need pattern (elderly, mobility-limited, home delivery) recurring independently in two different households -- not the same person or event.

pairs.text_a: When will the aid center reopen? Just checking.
pairs.text_b: Would like extra hygiene kits if any are available, no rush
pairs.note: Two unrelated low-priority informational/supply asks -- an easy, non-near-miss contrast pair.

pairs.text_a: Trapped under rubble after the building came down, can't move my leg
pairs.text_b: General inquiry about the next food distribution schedule
pairs.note: Completely unrelated severity and topic -- obviously not a match.

pairs.text_a: Wound on my arm needs cleaning, not bleeding badly, can wait a bit
pairs.text_b: Broken window at our unit from the wind last night, otherwise fine
pairs.note: Same neighborhood, unrelated minor issues -- obviously not a match.

pairs.text_a: Three kids alone since yesterday, no adult present, need someone to check on them
pairs.text_b: Would like information about registering for longer-term aid support
pairs.note: Very different urgency and topic -- obviously not a match.

pairs.text_a: Landslide blocked the only road out of the village, nobody can leave
pairs.text_b: Same landslide is also stopping the aid truck from reaching us, we heard it on the road below the village
pairs.note: Same landslide/road-blockage event described by two different reporters at slightly different points along the same road.

pairs.text_a: Cardiac symptoms, chest pain and shortness of breath, need urgent help
pairs.text_b: My uncle is having chest pains and can't catch his breath, right here at the same corner store where the first call came from
pairs.note: Same location marker (the corner store) and matching symptom description -- a second witness for the same medical emergency.

pairs.text_a: Building fire on 9th Ave spreading to the next unit, need trucks fast
pairs.text_b: Fire on 9th Ave has now caught the building next door too, still spreading
pairs.note: Same fire, escalation update from a nearby witness -- still one incident.

pairs.text_a: Flash flood came through the gully behind our row of houses, water rising fast
pairs.text_b: Same gully flooding described from two houses down, water's at our door now too
pairs.note: Same flash flood, same gully, adjacent houses.

pairs.text_a: Dialysis machine at the clinic is down, my mother needs treatment within hours
pairs.text_b: Clinic's dialysis equipment failed today, several patients including my father need urgent transfer elsewhere
pairs.note: Same clinic, same equipment failure, two different patients affected by the identical underlying incident.

pairs.text_a: Unaccompanied elderly woman on 3rd floor can't get down the stairs, building has no power
pairs.text_b: There's an elderly woman stuck upstairs in a different building across the block, stairs are fine but she's too weak to walk far
pairs.note: Same vulnerable-elderly-resident need pattern, nearby but different buildings and different underlying cause (power outage vs. weakness) -- not the same incident.
